name: Lidded Poached Eggs (No Vinegar)
desc: Eggs slipped into barely simmering water and cooked under a lid so the tops set without vinegar, served on toast.

source.title: Easy Poached Eggs (no vinegar)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: Water, to fill a lidded saucepan halfway
Flaky salt and black pepper, to finish

steps: Fill a saucepan with a tight-fitting lid halfway with water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer (small bubbles on the bottom, surface barely moving).
Crack one egg into a small cup, then slide it gently into the water. Cover with the lid.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the white is firmly set and the yolk is still runny.

Lift the egg out with a slotted spoon, let it drain for a few seconds, and set it on the toast spread with cottage cheese or ricotta and topped with cucumber. Repeat with the second egg, then season with flaky salt and pepper.
tips: The lid steams the top so the egg holds together without salt or vinegar in the water.

If the whites spread into wisps, crack each egg into a small fine-mesh sieve first and let the thin white drain away for a few seconds before sliding it into the pan. Some versions of this lid method cook the egg right in the sprayed sieve.

references.title: My New Favorite Hands-off Method for Perfectly Poached Eggs
references.usedFor: the creator's sieve-and-lid method, sieve size, cooking spray, 3 to 4 minutes, doneness cue
